properties.name: An agent driving reflow2 from a terminal can have every read auto-approved while each write still asks: `reflow2 read <tool>` and `reflow2 write <tool>`
properties.statement:
Step 3 of the plan to make the `--call` door work for an agent that cannot use MCP (Anthony, 2026-10-01; his idea 4 in using_call.md).

Today every door call is a terminal command VS Code prompts for, and one auto-approve pattern cannot tell a read from a write.

MUST:
- `reflow2 read <tool> [json]` runs only tools whose served annotation says read-only, and refuses any other tool before opening anything.
- `reflow2 write <tool> [json]` runs the rest.
- Both default the design path to the project's own and keep logging quiet, so a rule such as `^reflow2 read ` is safe to auto-approve.
- The read/write split reuses the classification `--call` already makes (read_only_hint, main.rs ~757).
- A check proves every tool annotated read-only really writes nothing, because the annotation now decides what is auto-approved.
